open_points.subject: M15 guarded-edge skip rule
open_points.text: “A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node, is not executed and is recorded `skipped_by_guard`” is unqualified, while A05 phase 6 permits an input port to be supplied by a constant and therefore to have no incoming edges, and A13 rule 3 delivers that constant.
open_points.question: Does the new per-input skip test apply only to edge-fed ports that have at least one incoming edge, or does a constant-fed port with zero incoming edges satisfy “every incoming edge” vacuously and skip the node?
options: Apply the test only to ports whose source is one or more edges; a delivered constant makes its port available
Treat zero incoming edges as vacuously all disabled and skip even when the port has a constant
Define constants as incoming sources for this test despite not being FlowEdges
open_points.default_guess: Apply the test only to edge-fed ports and treat a delivered constant as available.

open_points.subject: A03 startup probe
open_points.text: “the start probe (rule 8) runs the same runner, so a host where the limit cannot be set does not start the kernel” does not state the `process_count` used by the probe, although the runner sets `RLIMIT_NPROC` to `process_count` plus one and contracts from an earlier release may retain bounds above the current release ceiling.
open_points.question: Which process-count value or set of values must the startup probe attempt so that its success proves every stored and newly issuable contract can set its required limit?
options: Probe at the greatest process count among the current release ceiling and all stored contract versions
Probe only at the current release ceiling
Probe every distinct process count used by stored contracts plus the current release ceiling
Use a fixed probe-only process count
open_points.default_guess: Probe at the greatest process count among the current release ceiling and all stored contract versions.

open_points.subject: A03 resource-exhaustion classification
open_points.text: “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`” and “the code runs without capabilities … so it can neither raise nor bypass a limit” do not define what observation proves that the new `setrlimit` process or address-space limit was hit when Python code catches the resulting allocation or process-creation error and returns conforming outputs.
open_points.question: Does a denied allocation or process creation count as `resource_exhausted` even when user code catches the error, and if so what runner-visible evidence records that hit and gives it precedence over success or another outcome?
options: Every denial caused by either setrlimit counts, and the runner must record it independently of user code
Only termination or another externally observable limit event counts; a caught error does not
A caught denial is ordinary program behavior unless it causes a trap or invalid output
open_points.default_guess: Only an externally observable limit event counts unless the runner has an explicit, tamper-resistant way to record the denial.

open_points.subject: A03 address-space limit setup failure
open_points.text: “address space by the parent, from outside the environment” is followed only by “A runner that cannot set its limit exits before loading the code and the execution is `crashed`”; it does not say what happens when the outside parent cannot set the address-space limit or exactly which process receives and inherits it.
open_points.question: Which process has `RLIMIT_AS` set, at what point relative to starting bubblewrap, and how is failure of that outside setup classified during the startup probe and during a later execution?
options: A dedicated outer launcher sets its own hard and soft limit before execing bubblewrap; setup failure makes the probe fail at startup and makes a later execution `crashed`
The kernel parent applies a limit to the already-created sandbox process; failure is `crashed`
Failure to install the address-space limit is an internal error that stops the kernel rather than an execution outcome
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated outer launcher that sets the inherited limit before execing bubblewrap; fail startup during the probe and classify a later setup failure as `crashed`.
